Septal cells are more numerous than type I cells, although they do not cover nearly as much surface area as do type I cells. alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Patency of the trachea and primary bronchi is maintained by a series of hyaline cartilage rings. As bronchi decrease in diameter to become secondary bronchi, the rings are replaced by hyaline cartilage plates, as seen here. A perichondrium surrounds each plate.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Olfactory epithelium (classified as pseudostratified columnar with cilia) of the olfactory region in the nose is much thicker than is respiratory epithelium, seen on the opposite surface. In addition to the usual epithelial cells, bipolar neurons are also present. Their nuclei are located in the middle of the epithelium with nuclei of supporting cells above and those of basal cells below the neuronal nuclei.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. A secondary bronchus resembles a primary bronchus except that all layers are thinner; the passageway is surrounded by plates rather than rings of cartilage; and the smooth muscle becomes more prominent. Abundant, longitudinal elastic fibers remain in the lamina propria, but they are more dispersed than in the trachea and primary bronchi.

alternativas.feedback: CORRRECT. Broncholes lack cartilage plates and mixed glands. In large bronchioles, such as the one seen here, the epithelium remains pseudostratified columnar with cilia and goblet cells; the lamina propria contains a smooth muscle layer represented as bands spiralling around the bronchiole. Other changes occur as the passageway decreases in diameter.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Visceral pleura covers the exterior surface of the lung, lining the interior surface of the pleural cavity and sending septa into lung tissue proper. Pleura is composed of a mesothelium (simple squamous epithelium) and an underlying connective tissue containing elastic fibers and blood vessels.
